A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpatialDreamer and provide readable, matchable text, equations, figures, and tables. V1 ends with references despite mentioning supplementary results; v2 includes supplementary Sections 6–7. The comparison assesses material present in the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: V1 reports original stereo image and video synthesis results, quantitative comparisons, and component ablations in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–8.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds runtime measurements, depth and motion sensitivity results, and further ablations in supplementary Tables 4–7.

M1.justification: V2 redraws TIL within RefinerNet, narrows removal/training wording to its cross-view attention in Section 3.5, and changes the stated inference-view roles in Figure 2's caption. The components and equations remain unchanged. The PDFs leave uncertain whether these changes revise the procedure or correct its description.

E1.justification: Both versions use RealEstate10K and the same self-collected monocular-video dataset for stereo image and video synthesis. Additional qualitative examples and estimator configurations do not establish a new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: V2 adds MVSplat to the quantitative video comparison in Table 2; v1 evaluated it only in the image comparison. The existing image and video comparator sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds a runtime protocol using 1024×1024, 30-frame videos on an A800 GPU, motion-estimator comparisons, and DepthCrafter configurations with DVG/TIL controls. The existing 1,400/100 video split, eight-frame training clips, training budgets, and main accuracy metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component ablations and stated depth-estimator comparison, v2 supplies quantitative motion-estimator sensitivity in Table 5, depth-estimator sensitivity in Table 6, and a DVG/TIL ablation using DepthCrafter in Table 7. Supplementary Figures 10–11 add visual evidence. This substantially expands evidence about component dependence and robustness.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: The original numerical entries in Tables 1–3 are retained, while Table 2 adds MVSplat with FVD 1543 and warping error 7.913×10⁻³. Tables 4–7 add substantial runtime, sensitivity, and ablation results, including FVD 62.50 with DepthCrafter. That result uses a different depth configuration and does not establish a same-setting improvement over the retained MiDaS result of 67.09.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, including occlusion refinement, temporal attention aggregation, stereo deviation strength, and training losses, are retained. Naming the existing reconstruction loss adds explanation; no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: self-supervised stereo-video synthesis using DVG, RefinerNet, and consistency control, with claimed superiority over existing methods. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 4.6 identifies dependence on depth accuracy/distribution and model size as a barrier to real-time use, and suggests implicit depth as future work. Section 6.3 interprets differences between depth estimators. Section 4.4 newly claims a MVSplat advantage at t=10; Table 1 supports that comparison for PSNR/SSIM but not LPIPS.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project URL, a supplementary video-file guide, the 2.485-billion parameter count, and a DVG/inference runtime breakdown. Table 1 explains the t=5/10 frame offsets. Conversely, v1's explicit statement that methods share camera matrices and poses is omitted, without establishing a protocol change.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to DepthCrafter for depth-estimation experiments and Wonderland for the suggested implicit-depth direction. Existing references and the main positioning against prior synthesis methods are retained.

P1.justification: V2 tightens passages in the abstract, introduction, related work, and method description, updates affiliations and corresponding-author information, and adds limitations and supplementary sections. The main narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 2, revises an example in Figure 6, and relocates Tables 1–3 and Figure 7. New supplementary tables and extensive image/video comparison grids substantially expand the visual presentation. Figures 9–10 include both enlarged existing examples and additional cases.

improvement.justification: Tables 4–7 and the supplementary figures make computational cost, estimator sensitivity, and component effectiveness more assessable, while Section 4.6 adds concrete applicability limits. These improve the evidence supporting the retained main results. Ambiguous method-description revisions and imprecise MVSplat comparison wording limit the overall gain.
